title: Conseiller Technique_ Surveillance Epidémiologique et Santé Sécuritaire
description: Overview Jhpiego recrute Pour le compte de l’ Unité de Gestion Opérationnelle (UGO) de l’Accord de Coopération entre le Gouvernement de Côte d’Ivoire et le Gouvernement des Etats-Unis d’Amérique Poste : Conseiller Technique_ Surveillance Epidémiologique et Santé Sécuritaire Unité : Unité de Gestion Opérationnelle (UGO) DGS/MSHP CMU Côte d’Ivoire Superviseur : Responsable Technique Programmatique Supervisés : Aucun Lieu d’affectation : Abidjan Type de contrat : Contrat à durée déterminée (CDD) / Cadre Moyen Date limite de soumission : Lundi 31 août 2026 à 17H30 Critère spécifique : Poste ouvert aux nationaux ivoiriens NB : Les candidatures seront examinées au fur et à mesure de leur réception. Le processus de sélection pourra être engagé avant la date limite de dépôt des candidatures. Résumé : Sous la supervision du Responsable Technique Programmatique, le Conseiller Technique_ Surveillance Epidémiologique et Santé Sécuritaire contribue à la mise en œuvre des activités de surveillance épidémiologique, de préparation et de réponse aux urgences sanitaires en coordination avec les parties prenantes nationales Il appuie le développement des compétences en épidémiologie de terrain, le suivi des systèmes de surveillance, l'analyse des données et la coordination des interventions visant à renforcer la sécurité sanitaire et l'approche One Health (Une seule Santé). Responsibilities Spécifiquement, le/la titulaire assurera les responsabilités suivantes : Coordination technique et renforcement des capacités (70%) Appuyer la mise en œuvre des activités de surveillance épidémiologique et de sécurité sanitaire. Contribuer à la coordination des activités de formation et de mentorat des participants. Participer à la planification et au suivi des activités liées à l'approche One Health et aux activités de prévention, de détection, et de ripostes face aux épidémies. Collaborer avec l’INHP, et les autres structures partenaires de la plateforme UNE SEULE SANTE, pour renforcer les systèmes de surveillance et les actions de ripostes. Appuyer l'élaboration des outils, guides, procédures et supports techniques de surveillance, détection et riposte y compris aux portes d’entrées. Suivi, Évaluation et Renforcement des Capacités (30%) Assurer le suivi des activités de la plateforme UNE SEULE SANTE pour le compte de l’UGO. Participer aux investigations épidémiologiques, supervisions et évaluations sur le terrain. Faciliter l’analyse des données et produire des rapports et des bulletins tels que requis. Suivre les indicateurs de surveillance et documenter les alertes de santé publique. Contribuer au suivi de la mise en œuvre des recommandations issues des investigations et missions de supervision. Required Qualifications Formation Doctorat en médecine. Diplôme en Épidémiologie, Santé Publique, Biostatistique. Expérience Minimum cinq (5) années d'expérience dans la surveillance épidémiologique, la santé publique ou la gestion des urgences sanitaires. Expérience en investigation d'épidémies. Expérience dans des projets financés par des partenaires techniques et financiers internationaux constituant un atout. Expérience dans le suivi-évaluation et l'analyse des données logistiques souhaitée. Compétences Techniques Bonne connaissance du système national de surveillance épidémiologique. Maîtrise de l'analyse et de l'interprétation des données. Connaissance de l'approche UNE SEULE SANTE et de la sécurité sanitaire. Connaissance des programmes de santé publique (VIH, paludisme, santé maternelle et infantile…). Excellentes capacités d'analyse et de rédaction de rapports. Aptitudes personnelles et professionnelles Intégrité et sens élevé de l'éthique. Rigueur et sens de l'organisation. Aptitude à travailler en équipe multidisciplinaire. Langues : Maîtrise parfaite du français (écrit et parlé). Atouts Expérience de travail avec les programmes nationaux de santé et les structures du MSHP-CMU. Expérience en coordination de projets financés par le Gouvernement des États-Unis d'Amérique ou d'autres bailleurs internationaux. Bonne connaissance des approches de renforcement des systèmes de santé, de durabilité des interventions et d'intégration des programmes. CONDITIONS DE TRAVAIL Disponibilité Engagement à respecter les règles de conformité strictes du département d’Etat du gouvernement des Etats-Unis d’Amérique basée sur l’intégrité, la lutte contre la fraude, la protection des données, le code de bonne conduite. Conformité aux exigences de diligence raisonnable (vérification des antécédents, déclaration d’intérêts).

title: Immunization Program Advisor (anticipatory recruitment)
description: Overview Jhpiego is an international, non-profit health organization affiliated with Johns Hopkins University. Jhpiego works with health experts, governments, and community leaders to increase access and options to high-quality health services and health technology for their people. Through our partnerships, we aim to revolutionize health care for people who are disadvantaged and vulnerable around the world. Responsibilities The Program Advisor for Immunization will provide technical leadership and strategic guidance for implementation of priority immunization activities under the Gavi 6.0 portfolio in the Philippines. The advisor will support the Department of Health (DOH), local government units (LGUs), and immunization partners to strengthen immunization systems, improve data quality and use, conduct HPV vaccine coverage assessment activities, support evidence-based program improvement, and advance advocacy for new vaccine introductions, including Respiratory Syncytial Virus Vaccine (RVV). Under the supervision of the Country Program Manager, the Program Advisor will ensure the program, technical, and methodological quality of project activities and provide leadership in the design, implementation, monitoring, evaluation, and dissemination of immunization-related interventions in collaboration with the country team and global technical backstopping. RESPONSIBILITIES: Strategic Programmatic Leadership Provide overall technical leadership for Gavi 6.0 immunization activities in coordination with the DOH, regional health offices, LGUs, and partners. Regular communication with Jhpiego HQ technical and program management team. Support the development, implementation, monitoring, and periodic review of project workplans, timelines, deliverables, and technical strategies. Provide evidence-based technical guidance on routine immunization, HPV vaccination, immunization program performance, and new vaccine introduction. Serve as a key technical resource and advisor to national and subnational stakeholders on immunization program strengthening. Immunization Data Systems Strengthening Provide technical support and capacity building for immunization information systems, data automation initiatives, routine monitoring, and program review processes. Strengthen data analysis, interpretation, visualization, and use for evidence-based decision-making at national and subnational levels. Support the development and implementation of tools, dashboards, and reporting mechanisms to improve the quality and timeliness of immunization data. Mentor government and partner staff in routine performance monitoring and data-driven program management. HPV Vaccine Coverage Assessment Support the establishment and functioning of a Technical Advisory Group composed of representatives from DOH, WHO, UNICEF, academic institutions, professional societies, and other relevant stakeholders. Provide technical leadership in the design, development, and approval of HPV vaccine coverage assessment protocols and methodologies. Coordinate the collection, consolidation, validation, and analysis of HPV vaccination data from national, regional, and local sources. Lead assessments to identify barriers and facilitators affecting HPV vaccine uptake through stakeholder consultations, interviews, focus group discussions, and field validation activities. Support implementation of field data collection activities in selected regions and LGUs, including record reviews, health facility assessments, and key informant interviews. Ensure quality assurance and adherence to established protocols throughout coverage assessment activities. Prepare technical reports, presentations, policy briefs, and recommendations based on assessment findings. Disseminate findings and recommendations to DOH, LGUs, immunization partners, and other stakeholders to guide program improvement and policy decisions. Stakeholder Engagement and Advocacy Develop and maintain strong working relationships with DOH, regional health offices, LGUs, development partners, professional associations, academic institutions, and civil society organizations. Support advocacy and engagement activities with professional bodies and key stakeholders to facilitate evidence-based decision-making and support RVV introduction. Represent the project in technical working groups, advisory committees, immunization forums, and partner coordination meetings. Review and provide technical feedback on advocacy materials, communication products, training resources, and stakeholder engagement strategies. Capacity Building Provide technical content and support for trainings, mentoring, coaching, and orientation activities for government staff and immunization stakeholders. Strengthen local capacity in immunization program monitoring, data analysis, coverage assessment methodologies, and evidence use. Other Responsibilities Contribute to project reporting, documentation of lessons learned, and dissemination of best practices. Perform other technical and programmatic tasks as assigned by the Country Program Manager. Required Qualifications Required Qualifications, Experience and Skills Advanced degree in Public Health, Medicine, Epidemiology, Health Informatics, Biostatistics, Health Systems, or a related field. Minimum 7 to 10 years of progressively responsible experience in immunization, public health, epidemiology, health systems strengthening, monitoring and evaluation, or related areas. Demonstrated experience supporting national or subnational immunization programs in the Philippines. Experience with vaccine introduction, vaccine coverage assessments, immunization program evaluations, or related research activities preferred. Strong knowledge of the Philippine health system, Department of Health structures, and LGU service delivery mechanisms. Experience in data management, data quality improvement, routine health information systems, and data analytics. Proven experience designing and implementing field assessments, surveys, or public health research activities. Demonstrated ability to engage effectively with government agencies, multilateral organizations, professional societies, academic institutions, and development partners. Excellent analytical, report writing, presentation, and communication skills. Excellent oral and written English skills; proficiency in Filipino is highly desirable. Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a multi-stakeholder environment. Willingness and ability to travel throughout the Philippines, approximately 30-50% of the time. Preferred Qualifications Preferred Qualifications Experience working with Gavi-supported initiatives. Experience collaborating with DOH National Immunization Program, WHO, UNICEF, and other immunization partners. Familiarity with digital health systems, data automation, and routine immunization monitoring platforms. Experience supporting HPV vaccine introduction, adolescent immunization programs, or new vaccine introductions.

title: Consultant to Develop Rwanda Malaria Training Manuals
description: Overview Rwanda Ministry of Health and Rwanda Biomedical Centre (RBC), through Malaria and Other Parasitic Diseases Division (MOPDD), seeks to strengthen the capacity of healthcare workers to deliver high-quality malaria diagnosis and treatment services. Updated training manuals are required to reflect Rwanda Malaria Strategic Plan(NSP) 2027–2030, national malaria treatment guidelines, and Rwanda Multiple First-Line Therapy (MFT). The training manuals will support continuous professional development by promoting self-directed learning, facilitating structured knowledge and skills sharing, and ensuring standardized training for health workers across all levels of the health system Objective Overall objective is to develop and standardize malaria training manuals in line with current national malaria policies and guidelines to enhance knowledge, skills, and competencies of healthcare workers in delivering high-quality malaria diagnosis and treatment services across all levels of the health system. Responsibilities Over a period of 45 working days , the consultant shall: Conduct a rapid desk review of national malaria policies, relevant program documentation and consult with key stakeholders including Ministry of Health, RBC/Malaria and Other Parasitic Diseases Division, and implementing partners, Align training manual content with current Rwanda Malaria Strategic Plan 2027–2030 and Integrated Malaria Control Guidelines Integrate Rwanda's Multiple First-Line Therapy (MFT) strategy into all relevant training modules. Prepare facilitator guides and participant workbooks and ensure compatibility with the national Learning Management System (LMS). Develop competency-based assessment tools, including pre-tests, post-tests, clinical skills checklists, and case studies. Ensure training modules and content are designed to different targeted groups including Kinyarwanda content for CHWs, English and French languages for facility level providers Ensure Validation of the training manuals through stakeholder consultation Expected Deliverables The consultant will deliver a comprehensive, validated, and standardized malaria training package aligned with Rwanda Malaria Strategic Plan (NSP) 2027–2030, Integrated Malaria Control Guidelines, and Multiple First-Line Therapy (MFT) strategy. These include: Desk Review Report summarizing key findings from the review of national malaria policies, guidelines, strategies, and relevant program documents (5 days). Developed Malaria Training Manuals designed for different cadres of health workers, with content adapted for target audiences, including Kinyarwanda materials for Community Health Workers (CHWs) and English versions for facility-based healthcare providers (18 days). Facilitator Guides and Participant Workbooks designed to support effective training delivery and learner engagement, structured for integration into the national Learning Management System (LMS) (8 days). Stakeholder-Validated Final Training Package , incorporating feedback from the Ministry of Health, RBC/MOPDD, and key implementing partners, ready for national rollout and capacity-building initiatives (4 days). Standardized Training PowerPoint Presentations for each target audience (national, district, health facility, and community levels), professionally designed with facilitator notes and speaker guidance, and ready for immediate use with minimal adaptation for training and cascade implementation (7 days). Final Consultancy Report documenting the methodology, stakeholder consultations, revisions made, validation process, and recommendations for implementation and future updates (3 days). Management and Reporting: The consultant will be contracted by Jhpiego Rwanda and will report directly to the Jhpiego RISE Malaria Director, with oversight and technical input from Rwanda Biomedical Centre (RBC), Malaria and Other Parasitic Diseases Division. Required Qualifications Postgraduate degree in Medicine, Public Health, Medical Education, Infectious Diseases, or related field. At least 10 years of experience in malaria case management, health worker training, or curriculum development. Demonstrated experience in developing training materials and e-learning courses. Strong knowledge of Rwanda's malaria program policy , and WHO malaria guidelines. Experience with Learning Management Systems (e.g., Moodle). Excellent facilitation, communication, and technical writing skills. Application submission deadline: August 16th, 2026 Note: interested consultant shall sign, compile and submit the following as a single document: A detailed CV outlining relevant experience A cover letter expressing interest and availability A technical proposal with details A financial proposal in Rwandan Francs (RWF), clearly indicating the consultant’s proposed daily rate and the total professional fees for the entire assignment. Submission of all the above-required documents is mandatory. Failure to provide any of the required documents will result in disqualification.
